narrative: Material PL2__MD886B0A shows erratic demand (CV=0.62) with a mean of 239 units/day and no discernible trend over the observation window Mar-2025 to Mar-2026. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.40, mean 3.01 days), with lead-time variability contributing 55.5% of the demand-during-leadtime variance. The recommended (r,Q) continuous-review policy raises safety stock from 156 to 634 units to properly buffer the combined demand and lead-time risk, while consolidating 160 small annual orders into 30 large batches — reducing total annual inventory cost by 68.7%. The EOQ-optimal batch of 3,033 units is constrained to 2,029 by the 2,663-unit storage limit; this binding capacity constraint should be reviewed if throughput grows.
warnings: Removed 1 extreme lead-time outlier (18.82 days, >3 sigma from mean)
EOQ of 3,033 units capped to 2,029 due to max_storage_units=2,663 constraint — capacity constraint is binding; service coverage slightly below unconstrained optimum
SAP safety lead time (4.5 days) exceeds recommended value (2.65 days) — recommend reducing in ERP

research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic demand (CV=0.62) with moderate lead-time variability calls for a continuous-review trigger rather than a periodic review policy, ensuring replenishment fires precisely when stock hits the ROP regardless of calendar schedule. EOQ provides the cost-minimising fixed batch size given high ordering cost relative to low holding cost rate.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage capacity cap of 2,663 units reduces the order quantity from the unconstrained EOQ of 3,033 to 2,029 units, increasing order frequency from ~20 to ~30 per year and adding approximately $750/year in ordering costs vs. the unconstrained solution. If annual demand grows beyond ~60,000 units, the constraint will become increasingly costly and a capacity expansion or second storage location should be evaluated.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (374) + safety stock (634) = 1,008 units, which is well within max_storage_units (2,663). No MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
